description: Discover the 12 best NHL logos of all time in 2026. A designer's analysis of hockey's most iconic team brands.
body:
Introduction

Today, I'm going to the New York Rangers vs. Vegas Golden Knights game and as a logo designer—I couldn't help but analyzed the logo designs of NHL teams.

Great logos tell a story: they capture local culture, team history, and the spirit of the sport in just a few shapes and colors.

With that in mind, I’ve put together a list of some of my favorite NHL team logos—from timeless classics to newer, cutting-edge designs.

12 Best NHL Logos:

  1. New York Rangers‍
  2. Vegas Golden Knights‍
  3. ‍Florida Panthers
  4. ‍Nashville Predators
  5. ‍Dallas Stars‍
  6. ‍Tampa Bay Lightning‍
  7. ‍Pittsburgh Penguins
  8. Philadelphia Flyers
  9. ‍Hartford Whalers
  10. ‍Chicago Blackhawks‍
  11. ‍Seattle Kraken
  12. ‍Toronto Maple Leafs

I've broken them down by design elements together with my personal opinion on what makes each one stand out.

1. New York Rangers

Founded in 1926, the New York Rangers quickly became one of the NHL’s “Original Six” franchises.

Their success in 1928 made them the first American team to win the Stanley Cup, planting hockey’s roots firmly in New York City.

Over the decades, they’ve built fierce rivalries with neighbors like the Islanders and Devils, and continue to be an iconic presence at Madison Square Garden.

Design Breakdown

  • Classic shield design with 2 distinct notches.
  • Powerful, American red, blue and white color palette.
  • The name “RANGERS” set at 45 degree angle.

My Opinion

  • Timeless and distinct shape and color palette.
  • Minimalist, clean logo makes it look good on merchandise.
  • Diagonal text look iconic on jerseys.

2. Vegas Golden Knights‍

The Vegas Golden Knights are one of the NHL’s newest teams, joining the league in the 2017–18 season.

They shocked fans and pundits alike by reaching the Stanley Cup Final in their inaugural year.

Named to reflect Nevada’s historical ties to precious metals and the valor of medieval knights, they’ve quickly developed a loyal and passionate fan base.

Design Breakdown

  • A stylized knight’s helmet in regal gold, silver and black.
  • A subtle “V” for Vegas in the negative space.
  • Shield symbol stands for protection/authority.

My Opinion

  • Clean, bold and instantly recognizable logo.
  • The gold accent pops against the black.
  • Cleverly hidden "V" letter in negative space.

3. Florida Panthers

Established in 1993, the Florida Panthers were part of the NHL’s push to expand hockey’s footprint in the Sunshine State—Florida.

Their name honors the endangered Florida panther, native to the region.

They made an early splash by reaching the Stanley Cup Final in 1996, endearing themselves to the local sports scene.

Design Breakdown

  • A shield-style crest featuring a panther head in profile.
  • Color palette: navy, gold, red create military-like aesthetic.
  • Prominently displayed name on red background.

My Opinion

  • The modern design style make it look contemporary.
  • Still uniquely Floridian, but with a mature, refined style.
  • Great use of negative space and well-balanced colors.

4. Nashville Predators

The Nashville Predators joined the NHL as an expansion team in 1998, bringing top-tier hockey to Tennessee.

Their name and mascot were inspired by a prehistoric saber-toothed cat fossil found under a Nashville building site.

Over the years, they’ve cultivated a passionate fan base famous for country music–themed traditions.

Design Breakdown

  • A saber-tooth cat’s head in profile (predator).
  • Dynamic motion adds to cat’s fierce expression.
  • Unique color palette and sharp, aggressive lines.

My Opinion

  • Captures the team’s aggressive, high-energy style.
  • The angular look feels modern yet ties to ancient fossil origins.
  • Bright yellow/gold contrast well with dark navy blue.

5. Dallas Stars‍

Originally the Minnesota North Stars (1967), the franchise relocated to Dallas in 1993, dropping the “North” from their name.

They achieved a major milestone by winning the Stanley Cup in 1999, solidifying hockey’s presence in Texas.

The team’s identity continues to blend Lone Star State pride with a modern aesthetic.

Design Breakdown

  • A silver “D” for Dallas forming a star shape around it.
  • Unique color palette: victory green, silver and black.
  • The “D-star” is sleek, modern, and easy to place on jerseys.

My Opinion

  • The green stands out in the NHL, giving the brand fresh energy.
  • Merging the “D” with a star symbolizes both: team and state.
  • Overall, a clean, polished emblem that looks good on merch.

6. Tampa Bay Lightning‍

Joining the league in 1992, the Tampa Bay Lightning helped introduce hockey to central Florida.

They’re nicknamed the “Bolts,” tying in with Florida’s reputation for frequent thunderstorms.

The franchise has captured multiple Stanley Cups, solidifying their status as a powerhouse in the modern NHL era.

Design Breakdown

  • A simplified lightning bolt in a circle, set in unicolor.
  • Modern, minimal aesthetic with few extraneous details.
  • Occasionally uses a “BOLTS” wordmark for alternate jerseys.

My Opinion

  • Clean and bold; the lightning bolt is instantly recognizable.
  • Blue-and-white palette is classic yet stands out on the ice.
  • Probably the most minimalist logo, but still as impactful as others.

7. Pittsburgh Penguins

The Pittsburgh Penguins were part of the NHL’s 1967 expansion.

Their name was chosen to tie in with the icy conditions of the Civic Arena, nicknamed “The Igloo.”

A series of star players—Mario Lemieux, Jaromír Jágr, and Sidney Crosby—helped the team secure multiple Stanley Cup wins, endearing them to fans worldwide.

Design Breakdown

  • A cartoon-style penguin with a hockey stick.
  • The gold triangle representing Pittsburgh’s Golden Triangle area.
  • Sharp lines but also playful and iconic.

My Opinion

  • Balances fun character design with a strong sports identity.
  • The color scheme ties perfectly to Pittsburgh’s unified branding.
  • Beloved by fans, especially for its nostalgic tie to classic team eras.

8. Philadelphia Flyers

Joining the NHL in the 1967 expansion, the Philadelphia Flyers quickly made a name for themselves by winning consecutive Stanley Cups in 1974 and 1975.

Known as the “Broad Street Bullies” for their rough-and-tumble play, they have remained a notable force in the Eastern Conference.

Their rabid fan base and storied history make them a quintessential Philly team.

Design Breakdown

  • The winged “P” with an orange circle “eye.”
  • Distinct color scheme black, orange, and white.
  • Unchanged since its inception, a testament to its strong initial design.

My Opinion

  • One of the most recognizable letter-based logos in sports.
  • The P feels gritty, reflecting Philly’s tough reputation.
  • A great example of how a single letter can form a great logo.

9. Hartford Whalers

The Whalers franchise began in the World Hockey Association (WHA) as the New England Whalers in 1972.

Note that this is a Historic/Defunct team, which now became the Carolina Hurricanes, but the logo is so iconic—so I decided to describe it.

When the WHA merged with the NHL, the team moved to Hartford and became the Hartford Whalers.

Although they relocated in 1997 (becoming the Carolina Hurricanes), the Whalers’ brand endures as a nostalgic fan favorite.‍

Design Breakdown

  • A whale tail on top and an “H” hidden and "W" below.
  • Colors: green, blue, and white—fresh and maritime-themed.
  • Often celebrated as one of hockey’s best “hidden message” logos.

My Opinion

  • Iconic for its excellent use of the negative-space.
  • The playful color palette stands out among other NHL logos.
  • Lives on in throwback merch, proving great design can outlast a franchise’s actual run.

10. Chicago Blackhawks‍

As one of the NHL’s Original Six teams, the Chicago Blackhawks date back to 1926.

They were named after the “Blackhawk Division” of the owner’s Army Infantry Division.

They have won multiple Stanley Cups and are considered one of the league’s most storied franchises.

Design Breakdown

  • A Native American "Blackhawsk" head in profile.
  • Pretty detailed design in comparison to many sports logos.
  • Has become synonymous with tradition and legacy.

My Opinion

  • Visually striking and instantly recognizable (although could be simplified).
  • From a purely aesthetic standpoint, it’s one of the most artistic logos in the NHL.
  • Continues to spark cultural conversations about representation, reflecting evolving social awareness.

11. Seattle Kraken

The Seattle Kraken joined the NHL for the 2021–22 season, introducing top-tier hockey to the Pacific Northwest.

Their name references the mythical sea creature, nodding to the region’s maritime culture and folklore.

Despite being new to the league, they’ve quickly cultivated a dedicated following with their unique brand.

Design Breakdown

  • A stylized “S” for Seattle with a red eye.
  • Color palette: deep sea blue, ice blue, and red accents for contrast.
  • A subtle tentacle referencing Seattle’s nautical history.

My Opinion

  • Cleverly blending a single letter with a subtle creature element.
  • The layered blues evoke the depths of the ocean, setting the mood.
  • Already considered one of the best contemporary NHL logos.

12. Toronto Maple Leafs

Founded in 1917, the Toronto Maple Leafs are an Original Six franchise and a cornerstone of Canadian hockey.

The name pays tribute to Canada’s national symbol, the maple leaf, emphasizing national pride.

Despite a long championship drought, the team’s fervent fan base remains one of the largest in the league.

Design Breakdown

  • A stylized maple leaf in navy blue and white.
  • Features sharper edges and vein details.
  • The single-color logo looks good on merch.

My Opinion

  • Patriotic and instantly linked to hockey tradition.
  • Evolved without straying from its iconic roots.
  • A prime example of a logo that seamlessly blends national pride and local fandom.

Conclusion

Hockey logos blend team identity with local culture and a dash of creative flair.

From the timeless, shield-based design of the New York Rangers to the imaginative letter-art of the Seattle Kraken, each crest reflects a franchise’s unique heritage and aspirations.

Even historical gems like the Hartford Whalers continue to captivate design enthusiasts and fans decades after relocation.

But let’s not forget the NHL Shield itself—a monochrome emblem featuring a shield outline and diagonal lettering.

Originally introduced in 1917, it’s undergone a few updates, with the most recent version leaning into a sleek black-and-silver color scheme.

The league’s logo embodies the overarching spirit of hockey, providing a clean, authoritative backdrop for all these team identities we’ve explored.

It’s a fitting symbol for a sport whose branding can be as intense and dynamic as the action on the ice.
